role_E_zots.note: single rings isolated by aspect ratio (square within 10 percent); merged overlapping clusters excluded. The 26 and 28 px blobs in the probe set are false positives, not zots.

role_B_arrows.note: medians over the FULL blob population are NOT comparable - the count went 11 -> 23 as fainter arrows cleared the detection floor and dragged the median down. The well-formed cluster is the like-for-like comparison.

role_C_anisotropy.observation: growth is uniform (w 1.52, h 1.53). role C would have stretched ONE axis by 8x and is plainly absent.

the_1_50_coincidence: Two INDEPENDENT override families, measured in two INDEPENDENTLY FRAMED screenshot pairs, both land on raw 1.50. Both were authored as x3.0. A single common explanation covers both: the probe-pass shots sit one zoom step further out than the baseline shots, and 3.0 / 2.0 = 1.50. The alternative - that both families coincidentally grew by exactly half their authored factor - requires two coincidences and a mechanism nobody has proposed.

zoom_recovery.probe_frames_are: Z4 (73 px/tile), NOT the Z5 the filenames claim
zoom_recovery.strongest_datum: terrain tile-seam pitch 72.5 px baseline vs 36.4 px probe = exactly 146 and 73 px/tile, which is the quantity the question is literally defined on
zoom_recovery.controls: lens 1 resampled its own baseline to 0.5x Lanczos and recovered 0.4997 against a 0.5000 ground truth, proving it can resolve a one-step change rather than always saying 0.5; lenses 2 and 4 measured screen-space HUD chrome and got 1.0000. Amber exclusion was measured not assumed in all four (arrow pixels r-b = +57..+94, every landmark r-b = -16..-36, opposite side of neutral).

verdict.surviving_alternative: A contrived C-derived ~2.75 (33/12, the ratio of summed OccupantSize components) sits about 3 sigma from the width measurement rather than 12. Rejected on that plus the fact that an axis-blind sum formula would still be expected to leave some anisotropic signature, but a single max-zoom frame containing an arrow AND open ground would close it at >10 sigma by measuring the arrow in TILES inside one image.
